findings.before: Application, backup and migration accounts retained privileges on the obsolete PRD database.
findings.repair: Removed legacy schema/table/column grants and scoped service accounts to the two ERD databases.

findings.before: phpMyAdmin viewer had no failed-login lock policy.
findings.repair: Configured five failed attempts, one-day account lock, TLS and five concurrent connections; persisted in setup code.

findings.summary: ERD-only schema does not validate financial arithmetic/sign/quantity.
evidence: Negative service total accepted by ERD-only schema
Negative sale price accepted by ERD-only schema
Sale total can differ from subtotal and discount
findings.remediation: Add approved column CHECKs and backend validation/transaction rules after business review; keep the 7+5 table model unchanged.

findings.summary: A compromised application SQL credential can bypass session FK checks.
findings.evidence: Confirmed on a clone with the actual runtime principal, then rolled back.
findings.remediation: Keep SQL credentials in backend only; parameterize queries, forbid arbitrary SQL APIs, protect the OS and rotate credentials if exposed. Full mitigation requires a reviewed write API/stored-procedure privilege model.
